Class LOF<T>

java.lang.Object
smile.anomaly.LOF<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the data type of observations.
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class LOF<T> extends Object implements Serializable
Local Outlier Factor (LOF). LOF is an unsupervised outlier detection algorithm based on local density estimation.

Many outlier detection algorithms compare an observation against the global data distribution or boundary. However, in datasets where clusters have varying densities, points that are normal relative to a sparse cluster might be denser than outliers near a dense cluster. LOF addresses this by comparing the local density of an observation to the local densities of its k nearest neighbors.

For each point p, the algorithm determines:

  • The k-distance, which is the distance to its k-th nearest neighbor.
  • The reachability distance from o to p: reach-dist_k(p, o) = max(k-distance(o), d(p, o)).
  • The local reachability density (lrd), defined as the inverse of the average reachability distance of p from its neighbors.
  • The LOF score, which is the average ratio of the lrds of its neighbors to that of p.

An LOF score around 1.0 indicates an inlier with local density comparable to its neighbors. A score significantly greater than 1.0 (e.g., > 1.5) signals an outlier whose local density is markedly lower than that of its neighbors.

References

  1. Markus M. Breunig, Hans-Peter Kriegel, Raymond T. Ng, and Jörg Sander. LOF: Identifying Density-Based Local Outliers. ACM SIGMOD, 93–104, 2000.
